name: Why does grout crack and crumble over time?

mainEntity.name: Why does grout crack and crumble over time?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cracking grout is usually caused by movement in the framing underneath or improper deflection ratings in the subfloor, rather than a failure of the grout itself. When floors flex under foot traffic or wall studs shift during seasonal temperature swings across the Front Range, rigid grout lines absorb that stress and crack. Another frequent cause is improper mixing, such as adding too much water, which weakens the cured matrix. When repairing cracked grout, an experienced finish contractor evaluates framing support to ensure the movement stops before reapplying material.
acceptedAnswer.description: Grout cracks primarily due to subfloor or wall framing movement, excessive water used during mixing, or settling, which places stress directly on rigid grout joints.
